text: Living with heart failure?
There may be times when your symptoms get worse.
Call your doctor, nurse, or health worker
within 24 hours if your ankles, legs
or stomach swelling is getting worse,
which you can see when your shoes, socks,
or pants become tighter.
If your weight goes up or down by two kilograms in two days,
or it becomes hard to walk as far as usual,
or your breathing becomes more difficult,
check in with your health care team.
A new persistent cough, or difficulty sleeping,
with a need to use more pillows
to sit up and breathe calmly
are all warnings to ask for help.
Sometimes, your heart might be really struggling,
and you will need more urgent help.
If you experience the warning signs of a heart attack,
such as pain, pressure, heaviness,
or tightness in your chest, arm, back, jaw,
neck or shoulder, stop and rest.
If symptoms last more than 10 minutes,
call Triple Zero (000) and ask for an ambulance.
If you feel your heart racing,
and you're feeling dizzy, or you collapse,
call Triple Zero (000) and ask for an ambulance.
If you feel it is very hard to breathe, despite resting,
call Triple Zero (000), you need an ambulance.
If you are caring for someone
experiencing these urgent symptoms,
help them to rest, and stay with them.
Call Triple Zero (000), and ask for an ambulance.
And to learn more about managing heart failure,
watch the other videos in this series.
